name: DiceX Connect
author: dicex

sections.description:
Your store or site already knows when something important happens. Your phone doesn’t. DiceX Connect closes that gap: it listens for events in the plugins you already run and sends an SMS — to you, to your customer, or to both.

Nothing to wire up per event. Open the Integrations tab, switch a card on, choose who gets the message, and edit the wording. Every card ships with a sensible default message.

What you get

  • WooCommerce order notifications — a message when an order changes status, with the statuses you choose. Reads orders through WooCommerce’s own API, so it works on stores using High-Performance Order Storage.
  • Form notifications — WPForms, Contact Form 7 and Gravity Forms. A successful submission notifies you, and can notify the person who filled the form in.
  • Security alerts — repeated failed logins from one address, an administrator signing in, a new user registering, a password reset. Built on WordPress’s own hooks, so these work with no security plugin installed and keep working when you update the one you have.
  • The right recipients — a shared list of admin numbers, WordPress administrators who added a mobile number to their profile, or the customer the event is about.
  • Message templates you control — each card has its own text with tags such as {order_id}, {order_status}, {form_title} and {site_name}.
  • More than SMS — the same messages can go over WhatsApp, voice call, Telegram, Bale or Safir, depending on what your DiceX account has.

It stays out of the way

A card that is switched off registers nothing at all. A card whose plugin is not installed is shown greyed out, so you can see what is available without hunting for it. And if the gateway is unreachable, the failure is written to the plugin’s log — the order still completes and the form still submits.

It speaks your language

The plugin’s screens follow the language WordPress is already showing you, so there is nothing to configure. Every string is translatable and translations come from translate.wordpress.org, which means the plugin can appear in any language the community has translated — and a new translation reaches sites that already have the plugin installed, on its own.

The admin screens are built for right-to-left reading, so Persian, Arabic and Hebrew sites are laid out correctly. Iranian mobile numbers are understood however they are written: Persian and Arabic-Indic digits, +98, 0098 and plain 09 forms all work.

External services

This plugin relies on DiceX, a third-party messaging and payment service, to do anything at all. It is the only external service the plugin contacts, and it contacts nothing until you create a DiceX account and paste your own API key into the settings. Installing and activating the plugin sends nothing anywhere.

Every request goes to https://gateway.dicex.me/ over HTTPS, and carries your API key in a header so DiceX knows whose account it is.

What is sent, and when:

  • When you save an API key, open the Credit tab, or load the Sender lines tab: your API key. DiceX answers with the account balance, the plan, and the sender lines the account owns.
  • When a notification fires, or you press “Send test”: the recipient’s mobile number, the text of the message, and the sender line it goes out from.
  • When you start an online top-up: the amount, the bank you picked, and the address on your own site to return to after payment. DiceX answers with the payment link.

Nothing else leaves your site. The plugin adds no analytics, no tracking and no telemetry, contacts no other host, and loads no script, style or font from a CDN — everything it renders is served from the plugin folder.

DiceX links:

  • Service homepage: https://dicex.me/
  • Terms of service: https://dicex.me/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://dicex.me/privacy
  • Create an account: https://kyc.dicex.me/
  • Account panel: https://app.dicex.me/
  • API keys: https://dev.dicex.me/developers/api-keys
  • Top up, and where a coupon is applied: https://home.dicex.me/financial-operations/user-charge
  • What this plugin does: https://wp.dicex.me/

By connecting an account you are using DiceX under those terms, so please read them and the privacy policy first. The rest are ordinary links you click in the admin screens; the plugin sends nothing to them.

Bundled assets

The plugin ships one font: Vazirmatn, by the Vazirmatn Project Authors, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. The licence text travels with it in assets/fonts/OFL.txt. It is used for the plugin’s own admin screens because WordPress ships no Persian face, and it is served from the plugin folder — no font CDN is contacted.
sections.installation:
1. In your dashboard go to Plugins > Add New, search for “DiceX Connect”, then click Install Now and Activate.
  2. Open the new DiceX menu. It lands on Getting started, which links straight to creating an account and to fetching an API key. Paste the key under the Connection tab.
  3. Under the Lines tab, pick the sender line each channel should use, and send a test message to confirm it works.
  4. Under the Integrations tab, switch on the plugins you want notifications from.

To install manually instead: go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, upload the ZIP, click Install Now, then Activate, and follow steps 2 to 4.
sections.faq:
Do I need a DiceX account?

Yes. DiceX is a separate service, it is not free, and the plugin cannot send anything without an account and an API key of your own. Create one at https://kyc.dicex.me/ and read the terms at https://dicex.me/terms first.

Which channels can it send over?

SMS, WhatsApp, voice call, Telegram Bot, Bale Bot and Safir, depending on what your DiceX account and your region actually cover. Each card is given an ordered list of channels and tries the next one when the first does not get through.

Which plugins can trigger a notification?

WooCommerce, WPForms, Contact Form 7 and Gravity Forms, plus WordPress’s own login and user events, which need no other plugin. More are added over time.

How does it know the customer’s phone number on a form?

It reads the submitted values and picks the one that is a usable mobile number for your region. A field labelled like a phone field wins over any other. There is nothing to map, on any form.

Will a messaging failure break my checkout or my forms?

No. A send that fails is recorded in the plugin’s log and nothing else happens — the order is still placed and the form is still submitted.

Does it work with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage?

Yes. Orders are only ever read through WooCommerce’s own API, and the plugin declares HPOS compatibility.

Can my customers get messages too, not just the admins?

Yes. Each card chooses its recipients separately: a list of admin numbers, WordPress administrators with a mobile number on their profile, the customer or form submitter, or any combination.

What is the Region setting for?

DiceX does not sell the same services everywhere. The region you pick decides which channels and which payment gateways the plugin offers you. Nothing about it is sent to DiceX.

What languages does it come in?

The screens are English and follow your WordPress language. Translations are contributed at translate.wordpress.org and WordPress fetches them for you, so adding a language needs no new release of the plugin.
sections.changelog:
1.0.18

Corrects which channels can send without a line of their own, and adds two things people asked for.

Enhancements

  • Adds a note on the Credit tab for anyone holding a discount coupon, which has to be spent in the DiceX panel rather than here.
  • Adds a link to the plugin’s own page on the Getting started tab.

Bugfixes

  • Only SMS, voice calls and Safir can send on the DiceX shared line. WhatsApp, Telegram Bot and Bale Bot need a line activated on your own DiceX account, and the Sender lines tab now says which channels are ready and which are still waiting for a line, instead of promising a default for all six.

The releases before this one are in changelog.txt, next to this file.

screenshots.caption: Getting started — what DiceX is, which channels it can use, and the two ways in: create an account, or fetch an API key for one you already have.
The Connection tab — paste your API key, choose the region, and set the login code length, the voice call language and the name used in messages.
The Integrations tab — one card for each plugin DiceX can listen to. A card whose plugin is not installed is greyed out, so you can see what is available without hunting for it.
A card's settings — drag the channels into the order they should be tried, choose which order statuses send, pick who is notified, and edit the message.
The Sender lines tab — choose a line per channel, or leave SMS, voice and Safir on the DiceX shared line, and send a test message.
The Credit tab — top up online through Saman, Sepehr or Digipay.
